scenarioName: 036 - Severe Sepsis with Altered Mental Status

scenarioStory.history: Daughter reports patient has seemed "off" and increasingly drowsy since yesterday, with fever, chills, and decreased urine output over the past two days. This morning she was difficult to arouse and her breathing appeared labored. No reported trauma, no seizure activity witnessed.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a 73-year-old female in bed, febrile, tachypneic with labored breathing, and minimally responsive to painful stimuli. Daughter reports two days of fever and decreased urine output preceding today's decline. → Fluids and Access Started: IV access is obtained, blood glucose checked, and rapid isotonic fluid boluses are underway targeting a MAP of 65 mmHg. Despite initial fluids, the patient's mental status and labored breathing do not improve, and airway reflexes remain unreliable. → RSI Performed: With airway reflexes unreliable and mentation unimproved despite fluids, the crew performs rapid sequence intubation for definitive airway protection, using ketamine for induction given its relative hemodynamic stability in shock. → Tube Confirmed, Stable Transport: The airway is secured, ventilation and oxygenation are adequate, and the patient remains hemodynamically stable on ongoing fluids. Post-intubation sedation is maintained and the patient is transported with advance hospital notification.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Altered mental status and difficulty breathing

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a 73-year-old female in bed, febrile, tachypneic with labored breathing, and minimally responsive to painful stimuli. Daughter reports two days of fever and decreased urine output preceding today's decline.
relatedChecklist: Establish IV access (IO if 2 failed attempts or >90 sec); check blood glucose and full vitals
NS bolus 500 mL IV, repeat toward 2,040 mL (68 kg × 30 mL/kg) or MAP 65 mmHg
Provide advance notification to receiving hospital of suspected septic shock with impending airway management

scenarioEvents.name: Fluids and Access Started
scenarioEvents.description: IV access is obtained, blood glucose checked, and rapid isotonic fluid boluses are underway targeting a MAP of 65 mmHg. Despite initial fluids, the patient's mental status and labored breathing do not improve, and airway reflexes remain unreliable.
relatedChecklist: Recognize RSI indication: AMS with loss of protective airway reflexes, unresolved after fluids
Pre-oxygenate with high-flow O2 and PPV for at least 2 minutes prior to RSI
Fentanyl 68 mcg IV (68 kg × 1 mcg/kg) 2-3 minutes prior to intubation attempt
Ketamine 102 mg IV push (68 kg × 1.5 mg/kg, within 1-2 mg/kg range) for induction
Rocuronium 68 mg IV push (68 kg × 1 mg/kg) as paralytic agent
Attempt intubation, limiting each attempt to 15 seconds or SpO2 <90%, whichever first

scenarioEvents.name: RSI Performed
scenarioEvents.description: With airway reflexes unreliable and mentation unimproved despite fluids, the crew performs rapid sequence intubation for definitive airway protection, using ketamine for induction given its relative hemodynamic stability in shock.
relatedChecklist: Confirm ETT placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds; secure tube
Post-intubation sedation: Fentanyl 68-136 mcg IV (1-2 mcg/kg) plus Midazolam 1.4 mg IV (0.02 mg/kg)

scenarioEvents.name: Tube Confirmed, Stable Transport
scenarioEvents.description: The airway is secured, ventilation and oxygenation are adequate, and the patient remains hemodynamically stable on ongoing fluids. Post-intubation sedation is maintained and the patient is transported with advance hospital notification.

scenarioEvents.name: RSI Without Fluid Resuscitation
scenarioEvents.description: RSI is performed before adequate fluid resuscitation is completed. The combination of sedative-induced vasodilation, loss of sympathetic drive, and positive pressure ventilation on an unresuscitated septic patient precipitates abrupt, severe hypotension immediately after intubation.
relatedChecklist: Rapid NS bolus 500 mL IV, reassess toward MAP 65 mmHg goal
Norepinephrine infusion 3.4 mcg/min (68 kg × 0.05 mcg/kg/min), titrate to MAP 65 mmHg
